description: Erection of a single storey rear infill extension and elevational alterations to the lower ground floor flat alongside the erection of a single storey outbuilding in the rear garden
decision_conditions:
<p>All new external facing and roofing materials in respect of all the works hereby approved (and any other incidental works carried out in this connection) shall match those of the existing building in respect of materials used, detailed execution and finished appearance, including type, size, colour, bond, pointing, coursing, jointing, profile and texture.</p><p>

REASON: In the interest of the visual amenities of the surrounding area.</p>

The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of this permission.


REASON: In order to comply with the provisions of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended).

<div style="">Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (including demolition and all preparatory work), in accordance with BS 5837:2012 'Trees in relation to design, demolition and construction – Recommendations', a Tree Protection Plan(s) (TPP) and an Arboricultural Method Statement (AMS) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.</div><div style=""><br>The TPP and AMS shall specifically address, but not be limited to, the following:<br></div><div style="">Tree Protection Plan(s) (TPP):<br><ul style=""><li style="margin-left: 15px;">Precise location and specification of protective barriers to create a construction exclusion zone around retained trees.</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">Extent and type of ground protection measures where construction activity cannot be fully excluded from RPAs.</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">Details of any additional physical measures (e.g., tree protection boxes).</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">Clear indication of prohibited construction activities within tree protection zones.</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">Use of a low-impact foundation system (e.g. helical screw piles and suspended beam).</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">Careful excavation techniques and arboricultural supervision where required.&nbsp;</li></ul><div style="">Arboricultural Method Statement (AMS):<br><ul><li style="margin-left: 15px;">Methods for demolition and construction within or adjacent to RPAs, including details of specialized techniques (e.g., hand-digging, trenchless methods for services).</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">Location and installation of all services, utilities, and drainage, demonstrating adherence to RPA protection principles.</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">Details of any changes in ground levels and the design of retaining structures within or near RPAs.</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">Full specification for the construction of any new surfaces, including details of 'no-dig' specifications and relevant cross-sections within RPAs.</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">Specification for scaffolding and ground protection within tree protection zones.</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">Details of site access, temporary parking, on-site welfare facilities, loading, unloading, storage of equipment, materials, fuels, and waste, as well as concrete mixing and use of fires, ensuring no adverse impact on retained trees.</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">Methodology and detailed assessment of root pruning, if necessary, to be carried out strictly in accordance with BS 3998:2010.</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">Details of arboricultural supervision and inspection by a suitably qualified tree specialist, including the methodology and programme for reporting and a timetable for inspections.</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">Methods to improve the rooting environment for retained and proposed trees and landscaping.</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">Specific protection and management measures for veteran and ancient trees, if applicable.</li></ul>The development thereafter shall be implemented in strict accordance with the approved details.</div><div style=""><br>REASON: Required prior to commencement of development to ensure that trees to be retained are not damaged during demolition or construction, and to protect and enhance the appearance, character, and biodiversity of the site and locality.</div></div>

<p>Prior to commencement <span style="color: rgb(34, 34, 34); font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: small;">of the rear extension and outbuilding</span>, full details and specifications of the green roofs shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The submission shall include the following:<br></p><ul><li style="margin-left: 15px;">The design of the green roof should be in line with GRO’s code of best practice;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">Section drawings demonstrating a minimum substrate depth of no less than 80mm for a sedum roof;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">Details of the drainage system for the roof;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">Details of the planting mix, including a minimum of 9+ species for sedum roof;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">All roofs to be sown with a wide mix of species; the roof should not rely on one species of plant life</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">Management and maintenance plan, including access arrangements, irrigation, and general maintenance actions.</li></ul><div>The development shall not be undertaken otherwise than in accordance with the details hereby approved, which shall be implemented within a month of the first occupation of the development and shall be maintained for the lifetime of the development in accordance with the approved management and maintenance plan.&nbsp;</div><div><br></div><div><div>REASON: To promote biodiversity on site through green roofs, in line with Hackney's Local Plan LP33 policy LP46.</div></div><div><br style="color: rgb(34, 34, 34); font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: small;"></div>

<p>Prior to occupation, a Landscape Management Plan (LMP) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The LMP shall be prepared in accordance with the approved Biodiversity Gain Plan (BGP) and shall include details of a long-term management strategy demonstrating how the scheme will achieve and maintain Biodiversity Net Gain. The plan shall outline habitat creation and enhancement measures, including how these will be implemented and managed, with clear maintenance schedules, including weeding, mowing, irrigation, green roof maintenance, and management of trees.</p><p>Reason: To protect, enhance, and maintain the landscape features of the area.</p>

<p><span style="color: rgb(34, 34, 34); font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: small;">Following the removal of the tree as permitted by this decision, the tree shall be replaced by one of the same species in the same vicinity unless first agreed otherwise by the local planning authority.&nbsp; The replacement tree shall be planted during the planting season at the time of felling (end October - end March) or during the next immediately available planting season.&nbsp; The size of the tree shall be at least a Selected Standard as per BS 3936-1:1992 (or any standard that reproduces or replaces this standard).&nbsp; The tree shall be maintained for 5 years after planting, and should it be removed, die, be severely damaged, or become seriously diseased within this period, it shall be replaced with another tree as originally required to be planted by this condition.</span><br style="color: rgb(34, 34, 34); font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: small;"><br style="color: rgb(34, 34, 34); font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: small;"><span style="color: rgb(34, 34, 34); font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: small;">REASON: In alignment with policy LP51 in the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (2020).</span></p>

<p>Prior to the commencement of development hereby permitted, a Biodiversity Gain Plan (BGP) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.</p><p>The BGP shall set out how a biodiversity gain objective of at least 10% will be met, including:</p><p>● Information about the steps taken or to be taken to minimise the adverse effect of the development on the biodiversity of the onsite habitat and any other habitat;</p><p>● The pre-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat;</p><p>● The post-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat;</p><p>● Any registered offsite biodiversity gain allocated to the development and the biodiversity and the biodiversity value of that gain in relation to the development;</p><p>● Any biodiversity credits purchased for the development; and</p><p>● Any such other matters as the Secretary of State may by regulations specify.</p><p>When approved, planting of trees, shrubs, green roof, and plants shall be carried out within a period of twelve months from the date on which the development of the site commences or shall be carried out in the first planting (and seeding) season following completion of the development.</p><p>The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in full accordance with the details thus approved.</p><p>REASON: To ensure the development delivers a biodiversity net gain through both on-site and off-site delivery, in accordance with Schedule 7A of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, Hackney’s Local Plan Policy LP47, and London Plan Policy G6.</p>
